reviews.text: [h1] Isometric Risk of Rain 2 (Yay!) [/h1] [b] Four-Minute Video Review: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MgVP-Xf8HSU&ab_channel=MEGAthemicro [/b] Gatekeeper is a story-less, stage-based rougelite that gives you control of one of seven unlockable (you guessed it!) Gatekeepers, then asks you to murder everything in sight over and over again until you, yourself, are inevitably murdered. Repeat. Translation: it’s isometric Risk of Rain 2 without the timer. [b] SATISFYING GAMEPLAY [/b] Ardent fans of the roguelite genre will find little to no novelty on display in Gatekeeper... and that’s okay. Not every game has to be an innovation, but if it isn’t, it had better be pretty darn polished and mechanically tight. When it comes to combat, Gatekeeper is very much both. Dancing through the game’s dozens of lethal enemy types—often all of whom appear on screen at once (or so it feels)—and linking together devastating skill-based combos is a satisfaction I never grew tired of, probably because each run feels pretty different. In addition to the semi-random ordering of levels in Gatekeeper, the game gives you wide latitude to create new and interesting builds by prioritizing evolutions, skill upgrades, and artifacts. Evolutions occur upon leveling up, and doing so gives you the ability to choose between one of three stat boosts. Maybe you’re tired of getting one shot in later levels, so you focus on max health and regen rate. Or maybe you want to go all in on DPS, in which case it’s hard to say no to total damage and skill recharge. Whatever you do, don’t sleep on movement speed, as enemies get progressively faster as your run continues, to the point that you’ll be perpetually running for your life by the fourth boss (more on that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a bit). Every five evolutions, you’ll get to upgrade one of your four skills, and doing so intentionally can result in some powerful combos. For example, the mage Gatekeeper Pandora has a powerful lightning storm area of effect skill that pairs oh so nicely with the third stage of her dash ability, which goes from plopping down a small and short-lived AoE heal in stage one to a large and long-lasting damage multiplier in stage three. [b] A SENSE OF PROGRESSION [/b] But evolutions are but the appetizer, because the real fireworks (AKA “artifacts”) are found in the Emporium. It’s here that Gatekeeper injects that addictive roguelite sense of progression into its otherwise routine formula. By completing Emporium objectives, some of which are comically particular (“Die during the 42nd minute.”), you’ll gain the ability to unlock new artifacts. The more of these you unlock, the more they’ll appear during your runs, and if you don’t like what you’re getting, some levels feature a forge that allows you to convert them into something else. Artifacts can truly transform the battlefield. I went from [i] grinding [/i] down the game’s bullet-spongy bosses to melting them in seconds with an admittedly dangerous AoE artifact that forms by chance and takes 10% of everyone’s max health per 0.3 seconds, you included. Alas, if you're unable to pull off this gimmick or something similar, boss fights in Gatekeeper can turn into a real chore, and despite hours of attempts I have proven unable to beat the game’s fourth and final boss—a smokestack behemoth that can kill you in seconds from across the map. This means that I’ve only managed to unlock one new Gatekeeper, Pandora, after beating the game’s fun and frantic wave-based arena mode. Now, before you cry “Skill issue!” know this: after 10 hours of visiting new locations and unlocking artifacts, each of which helped elongate the next run, the game just outright deleted [i] all [/i] of the progress I had made, bringing my total number of unlocks down from around 40% to 0%. I’ve since confirmed it was due to a pre-launch patch (I got a review code last week), and it’s my [i] only [/i] complaint about Gatekeeper’s playability, as the game otherwise ran like a dream. [b] SOLID STYLE [/b] Despite the at times absurd number of enemies and explosive neon-colored particulate on screen, I found it easy to keep track of my Gatekeeper. This is a testament to the game’s visual design, not to mention excellent audio/visual telegraphing. For example, when those little death circles I used to exploit slow bosses form, the game will sound an ominous bell chime alerting you to their presence. And, as much as I hate him, that smokestack monstrosity does bellow a low rumble before firing off his infinite heatseeking projectiles. The game’s soundtrack is equally fun—a pulsing, bass-heavy electro jam that scales up or down based on on-screen intensity. [b] CONCLUSION [/b] In conclusion, Gatekeeper is a strange pre-launch patch away from being one of my favorite ever Early Access experiences. And that's without co-op, as I was unable to find anyone to play with during my review window. With a silly cheap price of $15 (currently $12 on sale), I think the addictive Gatekeeper presents above-average replayability and value. I’m giving the game an aggregate MEGA score (full scoring breakdown, from “Plot” to “Sound”) of 3.45/5 and welcome any questions about the game or my review. Thanks for reading! 游玩体验版后我认为的一些问题和一些建议： 1、这一点是对于我个人体验来说唯一的大问题：缺少自动保存功能。对于一些空闲时间可能不太足够的单机玩家不太友好，因为单人游玩完成一局完整游戏需要的时间并不算短，一般需要40-50分钟。我这里所提及的保存功能并非“保存当局游戏装备和数据供下一局使用”，而是“中途退出自动保存以供玩家随时在有空闲时间时，从之前退出的时刻继续同一局游戏”。最好能像《土豆兄弟》（Brotato）一样，单档位存档，只能保存当前一局游戏，中途退出的时候自动保存，该局玩家死亡，或者开始新游戏后，之前的存档自动删除。这样既允许单机玩家随时退出，也不影响游戏整体难度。 其他就都是一些皮毛了，是我根据个人游戏体验提出的小问题和建议。 2、画面有一点小问题。我在开启8×MSAA并将阴影和贴图质量调至“极高”档位后，在选择角色界面仍能看到角色的模型线条有些不平整，尤其在开启supporter pack之后显示的红色线条中的不平整会更加明显。 3、建议角色选择界面对各难度和各模式增加鼠标悬停时显示文本描述，方便玩家在游戏内就能明白区别，而不用到游戏外搜索或者查阅资料了解。 4、除了激活图腾的地图关卡事件丰富以外，其他的诸如歼灭和激活能量池的关卡略显枯燥。 5、建议增加一个查看地形的地图功能，或者仅仅增加一个“当前地图剩余补给点（我忘记游戏里具体叫什么了）数量”的实时统计值，显示当前地图上有多少玩家没有拿取的补给点，还或者可以在进入新地图时直接显示各补给点的方向，而不是靠近到一定距离才显示。这样可以防止玩家在一些略大的地图里漏掉东西，也可以让玩家不用为了不漏东西跑遍地图。 6、有些时候如果廓仑等地图边缘的方向标识在屏幕下方的话可能会被技能栏挡住，不仔细看的话可能会看不到。如果可能的话，建议设置一条隐形透明的、与技能栏上方水平平齐的线，并将地图边缘方向标识在屏幕下方的显示限制在这条线以上。 此外，个人感觉游戏的难度曲线设计很合理，即使是200%的难度下，不做额外的特意的刷级，也基本能保持游戏的顺畅进行。很喜欢该游戏的美术风格和特效，还有具有空灵和神秘感的音乐。希望游戏越做越好。 2024.5.15更新： 1、建议在游戏中技能文本内增加一个实时显示当前该技能对应的精确冷却时间上限的功能。 2、建议图腾充能地图中，开启图腾充能后， 可以在屏幕上某一固定区域类似TAB显示当前物品一样，显示目前图腾已激活的特殊事件。 2024.5.21： 建议给人造物品增加描述，在数据库或者游戏内明确标记某一人造物品能获得的上限数量，以免有想做“获得20个同一物品”成就时错误地熔炉制作了等级上限是19或者其他最大等级小于20的物品 全成就啦！催更 2026.4.12： 现在这游戏连存档都有了，很完美的游戏，闲着没事我就打开玩玩，很爽

全成就直接总结，内容少， 定价偏高，以目前的游戏内容卖40我可能都觉得贵。（我港区算上DLC一共127港币，纯怨种草） 优点是游戏跟雨中2很像，道具画面都有雨中影子，最开始的味很对，缺点现阶段全解锁的情况下道具也太少少少少少了。模式上普通模式一共就三大关九小关，竞技场打着能睡觉 貌似也没看到类似雨中里可以堆范围的清屏道具，导致后期伤害爆炸了， 但是还是不够爽的感觉 最后总结，处处都是雨中的影子就没法不比较了，以现阶段来看这个游戏目前在我这里是给雨中2做DLC都勉强的。 内容太太太少了 ！ 喜欢这个类型但没玩过雨中冒险2的直接买雨中冒险2，类型框架既然放在一块比了肯定大差不差，但是游戏体量重复游玩度现阶段都没法跟另一个比， 后续开发好了可能会改好评，差评原因就是目前体量配不上定价。
可操作性不高，平面战斗的游戏方式就已经决定这个游戏的上限了，不如雨中冒险2，且一层可获得的装备数量非常少，一点也不爽，非常想要退款的一集

这次更新毁了这个游戏，更新前与好友抽空玩上两把还是很欢乐的。如果要更新加内容，不如就像之前一样增加小型地图，多做几关出新的boss和守卫。这次的更新让我不得不吐槽：1、游戏节奏变得超级慢，多了很多无聊的刷钱时间，让人失去游玩欲望。2、这个新的大地图很坑，还不如原来三个小型地图。地图本来就暗，到处都卡地形，经常卡到一个地方被小怪堵死。而且地图太大，都找不到队友，失去了一部分联机游戏的快乐。3、每个关卡里不停的刷怪。更新前只要完成任务就不会再刷新的小怪。这样子让玩家怎么拿熔炉？好几次拿熔炉被打死了。4、怪物的难度变得太高，不平衡。之前200%的难度和朋友一起玩，只要不是运气太差都能过关。现在200%难度铺天盖地的小怪，还要站在一个小圈里做任务，前两关根本过不去，尤其4个人一起玩时，更是可怕。我觉得这次更新是失败的，让我们不想打开游戏
第二次修改评测，但还是差评，首先200%难度道具构筑对了确实是可以爽的，但是有用的道具太少，说实话如果开新档只解锁那几个道具就无敌了，然后就是恶性BUG，解锁马拉松需要通关16关，但是打了两次16关必卡死，恶心至极

The game keeps getting harder and harder with every update to the point where it isn't fun. Even with friends, getting past the first level can be way too difficult on 100% as the increased time it takes to complete the objectives gives the enemies too much time to get stronger while you are stuck with only a few items. The game needs to be less stingy with money and items, especially early on. Or just don't make the items on a planet cost money. Just let us go and pick them up and save money just for the store in between planets. The game used to be a lot of fun, but the drive for making the game more difficult has just ruined it.

This game is a piece of hot garbage, and here's why: - This game tries to be Risk of Rain 2, copying a lot of ideas and mechanics from there, but making all of it worse in, what I assume, an attempt to make it feel more "unique" and "different", but fumbling the execution. - it has achievement-based item unlocking system similar to RoR but some of the achievements are incredibly obnoxious and frustrating to complete, and on top of it, it doesn't even actually unlock the items in question for you, because you'll have to additionally grind a special currency to slowly unlock the new items that you supposedly have already "unlocked", and you also need to pay said currency if you want to ban the items you don't want from the future runs drop pool. You also earn said currency at a turtle's pace with getting 1 per stage cleared with very rare rng drops from random enemies. - most characters are borderline unplayable due to how slow and underpowered they are, melee characters being the worst offender; - Most character kits were very clearly designed without understanding the chosen isometric perspective of the game and how it affects the gameplay compared to 2D platforming of ROR 1 and 3D third-person of ROR 2. While playing, regardless of the character, you'll be constantly haunted by the feeling of wrongness and jank about the game's combat; - it can be pretty difficult to hit mobs with projectile-based autoattacks on most ranged characters, considering there is no lock-on or homing on the projectiles for most of them, leading to you missing about 70% of your shots on most regular mobs that aren't up close and right in your face; - you will find it pretty difficult to deal with most bosses on melee characters simply because they seemingly don't give you enough leeway for dodging their attacks or just straight up don't give you the chance or don't want you approaching them or they'll just damage you with some kind of DoT aura or a poorly telegraphed AoE shockwave that can easily get lost in tons of ♥♥♥♥ already flying around from all the regular mobs the boss summons to your location; - Most AoE-based character skills and items, including melee attacks, feel useless or incredibly restrictive in most situations simply because of their incredibly small AoE radius (there is a character that leaves a healing area at the end of their dash skill and an item you can unlock that gives a chance of creating a healing area after killing an enemy, but their AoE is so small that its way too difficult and punishing to try and make use of them, as you simply can't stay in place for a long period of time or you'll get spammed and overwhelmed instantly), said AoE-based skills usually do get an increased radius as one of the skill upgrades, but you get said skill upgrades fairly rarely and it can take you a while to get the oes you want in every run, and frankly, that AoE buff still won't feel like enough most of the time. Melee skills are also very slow at the start, forcing you to stack attack speed just to deal with enemies at any respectible pace. There are no AoE-buffing items that I am aware of, and even if there are, I haven't unlocked them yet and honestly don't have the patience to anymore; - some character skills just outright don't work or don't do what the description says (like the Acolyte's fourth skill that is supposed to "deal damage" as a baseline but only shows the fireworks of projectiles flying out of enemies and homing into you but not actually doing anything unless you upgrade it); - enemies are rather annoyingly designed and can easily overwhelm or oneshot you, with some boss attacks being very difficult to dodge and feeling unfair when at later stages of the run the game can just spawn multiple of them on top of you, especially given how underpowered your characters are as a baseline; - Game significantly lacks content. There is some stage variety with multiple possible maps per planet that are all layed out slightly differently and look cookie and quirky, but don't really feel too different to traverse or deal with enemies in. There is also only one boss per planet which means there is a predetermined order of the same bosses you'll have to kill in every run. All of these grievances I have had been there since the early access and absolutely nothing have changed after 1.0. They have very slightly addressed the content issue, as they should, by obviously adding more stuff and new playable characters to the game, but instead of reworking the old character kits to being less awful to play with or removing the stupid-ass ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grindy item unlock system, they only added some slight character visual customization tool that they want you to pay extra $$$ for. Cool, thanks, I guess.

200%难度用脚填的数值，玩家的数值是被限制的，敌人的数值是硬给的，禁CD怪是必须三个技能干掉或者只准平A干掉他，那么问题来了，哪个角色的平A能在200%难度的情况下清掉所有杂兵后把精英清除？答案是没有。迫击炮锁敌是锁脚的，站在地图角落锁全图的，黑球制导亡语是甩不掉的，局外升级是没有的，所以200%更加难打，跟雨中冒险一个模子，当你开的神器越多，你反而越难胡。 英雄是一个比一个有缺点的，诅咒卡拿了大部分时候负面效果是大于正面效果的，踩点主线大部分是debuff的（并且增长速度慢得让人感觉就是故意卡你时间不让你退款），推车主线是拖拉的，地图buff大部分是给debuff的，只有开箱拆塔的主线最好做也最舒服。 改好了就改好评，作为割草肉鸽限制比奖励多太多，未来可期

在经历了差不多一年的抢先体验阶段之后，《Gatekeeper》也终于是发售了正式版，首发35%的折扣国区到手也就仅有30多元，在线人数也是一度接近3000人，算是同时期内比较热门的新品肉鸽游戏了。本作是一款俯视角合作射击游戏，有着深度的局内构筑玩法，特效绚丽的技能特效，整体体验是十分爽快的！ [h1]扎实且丰富的肉鸽体验[/h1] 游戏主要有两个模式，一个是关卡模式，一个是竞技场模式，虽然核心都是打怪叠buff完成强力构筑，但体验上还是有些许不同。关卡模式下需要完成局内部分任务以解锁boss战，手动开启一些机关来触发接下来的出怪，这一设计虽增加了操作步骤，但也给予玩家短暂的喘息时间，让玩家有机会调整战术，重新规划战斗策略。 竞技场模式则提供一个节奏更快、战斗强度更高的模式。敌人密度显著增大，战斗场地相对狭小，玩家需要在有限的空间内，迅速应对四面八方涌来的敌人，战斗的紧张感和刺激感被推向了极致，当然对熟练度也有更高的要求！ 游戏提供了 9 个可选择的心门守卫角色，每个角色都拥有独特的技能组，可以随着进度逐渐解锁，技能组中的技能固定不可更改，这就要求玩家在选择角色时，充分考虑自身的游戏风格和喜好，或者是团队合作之间的玩法配合。游戏大部分的技能都需要手动预判瞄准来释放，同时也要走位来规避技能，操作感还是比较强的。技能上aoe伤害居多，技能特效设计的也非常华丽，构筑逐渐完善后满屏的技能特效光从视觉上就提供了非常爽的战斗体验！ 本作的局内构筑系统主要以可收集的人造物品为主，门槛很低但组合下来上限非常之高，涵盖攻击、防御、辅助三类，高达上百种，且每件物品自带独特词条，多个数量堆叠可叠加更高的数值，也可以通过特定物品组合激活更强的属性，让玩家的攻击输出达到一个惊人的水平。 这种丰富的道具组合和强化系统，让玩家在游戏过程中始终充满探索欲望，每一次获得新的 人造物品都像是打开了一扇通往全新战斗体验的大门，不断激发玩家尝试新的 BUILD 和战斗策略。 [h1]结语[/h1] 游戏目前没有什么实质性的优化问题，虽然本质上对于同类游戏来说没有什么颠覆性创新，但不管是玩法还是丰富的构筑系统都让这份体验更加扎实！ [quote=][b]评测出自：[u]网易 UU 鉴赏家培训计划[/u][/b] [b]感谢由[u]网易 UU 鉴赏家培训计划[/u]提供游戏[/b] [i][b]加速云存领游戏，满足热爱游戏梦！[/b][/i][/quote]

This game is a worse, top down Risk of Rain. It's fun for maybe 10 hours, just because you can try all the characters and rack your brain on how to make unique, fun, and good builds before realizing there aren't really any meaningful choices in the game because of balance issues and the items being generically bad "on hit do more damage" or "do more damage if they're close" or "gain health regen" types of items that have little combo or playstyle effect. The game also has some painfully slow moments. Like some of the objectives you can complete within 30 seconds and reward skilled play, and then some objectives take minutes and there's absolutely nothing you can do to speed them up. If this game and it's DLC were 3 bucks, it'd be an easy recommend for a cheap thrill. At 10-15 + 8, there are so many better games out there in the 20-25 buck range. The devs should be proud for releasing a polished game. But the actual game design suffers despite being a near carbon copy of it's inspirations. If you read this, please consider: - Making every objective rewarding from a skill perspective. The timed, stand in a circle objective makes me want to quit the game everytime because it takes noticeably longer than any other and it slows the game down drastically. - Remove or rework the on death AoE balls, they do so much damage and force you to move in a straight line away to not get hit that they simplify the gameplay to the point of tedium. They either need to do less damage so that you can tank several, or they need to be more interactive in terms of dodging. Those two things would go a long way in making the game not "unfun". Bigger changes would be: - Look at how easy it is to build characters in different ways with the same 200% viability. Hammer guy has a node that he does damage based on max health, haven't been able to get that to work. Turret guy has literally 1 way to build them that feels good. Shotgun boy has grenade matters nodes and I don't have any idea how you would get the grenade to matter, let alone consistently. The node system is at odds with the item system which neither enable easy and varied build crafting. - Look at any source of damage that is nearly unavoidable such as teleporting characters, the chasing balls, the offscreen explosions, and realize they completely invalidate some of the cursed items. If someone dies to something cheap it feels 10x worse than dying to failed scaling, failed builds, or to bad dodges.

Roguelite game that looks very good on advertisting material but in reality is pretty disappointing and devoid of content. There are big enemies, mini boss fights, chaos and visual clutter but that's about it. It's missing balancing, content, proper refinement of game mechanics and basically everything that would make a roguelite good. It's bleak and soulless but fun for first 5 hours or so, especially with friends. If you're a seasoned roguelite / roguelike / rogue genre fan then well you will be utterly disappointed the longer you play this for. If not, you'll most likely have fun here. Fair to mention that developers have officially stopped development for this game so there won't be any new content what-so-ever. Is it worth $15 bucks? Hell to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ no. Maybe $5 on sale. It feels like playing a failed product whose company folded half way through before deploying "that one update" that would completely change everything... or a well-refined demo prototype made to promote a kickstarter. The rest of my thoughts are catalogued below. --- Wanna feel like you're an indestructible god? Won't have that here. Epic boss fights? Also nope. Difficulty? If you see enemies being scaled up, dealing more to you and spawning in mass amounts then I suppose that's difficult. Interesting item synergies? Please, your expectations are just too high. It feels like it took big inspirations from few games in similar genre and then done absolutely nothing to improve upon, or even make them flow into the core concept of the game, mostly inheriting the negatives of whatever concept they're making use of. A mash of everything that ends up forming ultimate mediocrity from all roguelites you may know and love. I can hear you saying "Oh Ducky you're being too critical!". I thought so too and ended up playing for a bit longer and damn. There's only one really big boss fight in this game and it's quite lazy and barely poses a challenge. Then it just ends with 4 lines of dialogue and credits screen. Bruh. Not to mention that the 'final boss' itself can be fully cheesed just by getting above 50% Movement Speed and that's about it really. Same with Sirens which in here are like RoR2 bosses that guard the gateway to next map. Items provide nothing to synergize any character and ultimately it doesn't matter what character you play as, the meta is always the same. There's no ultimate fun build you can do, if you won't pick something specific then you fail, simple as. Whole game can be summarized to: +50% movement speed, +40% Max Health, As much Attack Speed% as you can cram in, Items that grant extra status effects on skill / on hit. Run around and attack. No, you can't build differently because you rely on the extra damage from the "On Skill" / "On Hit" items later on.

Wasted Potential.. Gatekeeper has a strong foundation. The core loop is fun, the combat can feel great, and co-op boss fights are genuinely enjoyable. That is exactly why it is so disappointing to see the game left in this state. My biggest issue is the co-op flow. Outside of boss fights, the game too often turns into a solo scavenger hunt. Players split up for objectives, then split up again for leftover enemies, artifact collection, shopping, and moving toward the next area. Instead of feeling like a team-based co-op experience, a lot of the downtime becomes individual cleanup and backtracking. After a boss dies, the game really should have done more to keep the pacing tight: clearing remaining minor enemies, pausing scaling immediately, making artifacts or shrines easier to reach, or opening shortcuts toward the exit. These changes would have made the game feel much smoother and more cooperative instead of dragging the run out with chores. The map design also often feels too cluttered and restrictive. There are too many barriers, awkward walls, and momentum blockers, especially for characters without teleport or blink abilities. Wider lanes, better vertical routes, post-boss shortcuts, or even a simple vault/hop over obstacles would have helped the traversal feel much better for every character, not just the mobile ones. What disappoints me the most, however, is that the game seemingly will not be meaningfully updated anymore and will remain with these issues. There were clear opportunities to improve co-op pacing, traversal, long-term replayability, and overall flow. The lack of native mod support makes this even worse. A game like this could have lived much longer through community content, balance tweaks, custom maps, new characters, or quality-of-life mods. Without continued development and without proper mod support, the game feels like it has been left with untapped potential. In the end, Gatekeeper is a game with a good core idea, but not enough polish, not enough long-term support, and not enough community tools to keep it alive. Not recommended, especially if you were hoping for lasting co-op replayability, meaningful updates, or modding support.
